dedupe_keys.name: nab study of the economic impact of local tv and radio broadcasting in the united states woods poole january 2024

description: This NAB press release summarises a study by Woods & Poole Economics, supported by BIA Advisory Services, of the economic impact of local commercial television and radio broadcasting in the United States, with information by state said to be in the study. The release reports $1.23 trillion of GDP and 2.52 million jobs from direct and stimulative effects, direct employment of more than 314,000 jobs generating over $55 billion a year (television 193,000 jobs and $34 billion of GDP, radio 121,000 jobs and $21 billion), 99,000 further jobs in supplier industries from an input-output analysis, and a ripple effect of nearly $139 billion in GDP and more than 784,000 jobs. Producer: NAB, the US broadcasters' trade association, releasing on 4 January 2024; the study itself was not read. Coverage: the US national economy and states. Access: a free public press release; the full study and state tables were not found on the page. Licence and cost: not stated; free to read. Caveats: an industry-commissioned summary, so the underlying methods and state figures cannot be checked from the page. Simulation uses: the employment and GDP multipliers give economic loss inputs for resilience studies of broadcast service disruption. Related record: the FCC Media Bureau broadcast station databases (data-fcc-lms-cdbs-broadcast-station-databases).
